tldr: El Agente Q is an LLM-based multi-agent system with a hierarchical cognitive architecture that dynamically generates and executes quantum chemistry workflows from natural language prompts, demonstrating >87% average task success across university-level exercises and two real-world case studies.
contributions: Introduction of El Agente, a novel hierarchical cognitive architecture for language agents integrating working memory, long-term memory (procedural, semantic, episodic), and an LLM reasoning core
Development of El Agente Q, an application of El Agente to automate quantum chemistry workflows including geometry optimization, DFT calculations, error recovery, and file I/O
Hierarchical multi-agent design with three functional modules: geometry, quantum calculation, and file I/O, enabling task decomposition and adaptive tool selection
Automated error handling and in situ debugging capabilities, including runtime error recovery and imaginary frequency resolution
Action trace export to Jupyter notebooks for reproducibility and workflow adaptation
methods: The authors designed El Agente Q as a hierarchical multi-agent system where a top-level computational chemist agent plans tasks and delegates to lower-level specialized agents within three modules (geometry, quantum calculation, file I/O). Each agent has domain-specific context, semantic memory, callable tools/modules, and delegates subtasks downward. The system was benchmarked on six university-level quantum chemistry exercises (covering geometry optimization, thermodynamic stability, and electronic structure analysis) and two case studies (solvent effects on IR spectra of alanine, and lanthanoid complex generation/optimization). All evaluations ran in fully autonomous mode with only one user input prompt. Success rate was measured as the percentage of successful runs out of 10 trials per exercise.
results: El Agente Q achieved an average success rate of >88.8% for Level 1 and >87.6% for Level 2 difficulty across all university-level exercises. Specific results include: Organic compounds (Level 1: ±10%, Level 2: ±17%), Inorganic compounds (Level 1: ±9%, Level 2: ±7%), Relative stability of carbocations (Level 1: ±18%, Level 2: ±13%), Ring strain of cycloalkanes (Level 1: ±7%, Level 2: ±11%), pKa of common acids (Level 1: ±16%, Level 2: ±16%), Absorption spectrum of organic molecules (Level 1: ±0%, Level 2: ±0%). The system successfully resolved ORCA runtime errors from hallucinated keywords, recovered from incorrect XYZ input file specification by switching to one-at-a-time submission, automatically corrected imaginary frequencies in cyclobutane and carbocation structures, and debugged energy convergence issues. In case studies, it correctly allocated 8, 16, and 24 cores for gas-phase, CPCM, and explicit-CPCM models respectively.
limitations: Episodic memory is disabled in the current implementation of El Agente Q
Performance variability exists across runs, with standard deviations ranging from ±0% to ±18%
Level 2 absorption spectrum exercise had 0% success, indicating challenges with unconstrained complex tasks
Hallucinated non-existent ORCA keywords (e.g., DOSINGLET, DOTRIPLET, NROOTS_TRIPLET) were initially generated before being corrected
The system sometimes requires iterative debugging rather than succeeding on first attempt
